DONE. Scheduler.submit(spec: LaunchSpec) — the phantom type parameter is gone.

Shape: LaunchSpec(submissionKey, name, source, arguments, resultContract: ResultContractDescriptor, resources, environment, array, retrySafety). Script-shaped, because a script is what a scheduler launches.

What actually changed semantically, which is more than type hygiene:
- ssh/Slurm.scala `erase` is DELETED. It accepted any JobRequest[A], rewrote the result contract to ExitOnly, and submitted successfully — so a caller asking for a structured result got a job that had silently discarded the request. LaunchSpec carries the descriptor, and the opaque submission codec now REFUSES a contract it cannot carry ("the opaque submission protocol carries only exit-only result contracts") instead of rewriting it.
- LaunchSpec.fromRequest refuses registered-task payloads with a typed diagnostic rather than pretending. Only the task layer knows the worker invocation, and RegisteredTaskLauncher:419-425 already lowers correctly with the contract preserved.

THE JOURNAL BREAK DID NOT HAPPEN, and that is worth recording because I asked for a decision on it. The wire was ALREADY launch-shaped: encodeSubmitRequest emitted a flat submissionKey/name/source/arguments/resources/environment/resultContract/array/retrySafety with the payload already destructured and the contract as a hardcoded "exit-only" string. Keeping that field set byte-identical was therefore possible while still fixing the defect — refuse rather than rewrite. Evidence: every golden fixture is unchanged in git, and both the observation-timing fixture and CanonicalRequest's decode/re-encode round-trip law pass untouched. Existing journals and the attempt identities derived from their digests remain valid. The approved break was not needed.

Also erased, since each existed only to feed submit and each read only untyped fields: SubmissionPlanner.prepare / PreparedSubmission (cli/CliModel.scala), SiteProfile.resolve, ManagedRequestPolicy.validate, PreparedLocalSubmission, ManagedController.submit, AgentApi.submitOpaque.

Added Scheduler.submitLowered as an extension for callers holding a JobRequest. It is explicitly NOT a return of the erased parameter — the result is still an untyped SubmissionAttempt and a non-lowerable payload becomes a PreparationFailed.

One test got better by losing an assertion: WorkerRuntimeSuite's capturing scheduler used to assert "registered task was not lowered to a script" in a fallback branch. A LaunchSpec is script-shaped by construction, so the type now answers that question and the test asserts WHICH script instead.

Verification: 21 implementations and 22 call sites updated across 10 modules. Full suite 411 (408 + 3 new LaunchSpecSuite) green on Scala 3.3.8 AND 3.8.4, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean, no golden fixture modified.

Follow-on for D2: PreparedJob[A] = LaunchSpec + ResultPlan[A] + content digest now has a clean seam to sit on. The typed layer was already independent — RemoteTasks never touched JobRequest and recovers A from SlurmTaskCall plus a runtime ResultSchemaId match.
